name: Euler totient function φ(n)
description: φ(n) = |{1 ≤ k ≤ n : gcd(k,n) = 1}|, counting the integers up to n that are coprime to n.

name: Asymptotic for the summatory Euler totient
description: ∑_{n≤x} φ(n) = (3/π²)x² + O(x log x), following from Möbius inversion and the hyperbola method.

name: Density of squarefree integers
description: The proportion of squarefree integers up to x tends to 6/π² = 1/ζ(2); equivalently ∑_{n≤x} |μ(n)| = (6/π²)x + O(√x).

name: Big-omega function Ω(n)
description: Ω(n) = ∑_{p^a‖n} a, the number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity; a completely additive function.

name: Mean value of ω(n)
description: ∑_{n≤x} ω(n) = x log log x + Mx + o(x) where M is the Meissel–Mertens constant; similarly for Ω(n).

name: Hardy–Ramanujan theorem on normal order of ω(n)
description: The normal order of ω(n) is log log n: for every ε > 0, the set of n with |ω(n) − log log n| > ε√(log log n) has density zero.

name: Turán's inequality for ω(n)
description: ∑_{n≤x} (ω(n) − log log x)² = O(x log log x), giving the variance bound that implies the Hardy–Ramanujan normal order result.

name: Legendre sieve formula
description: S(A,z) = ∑_{d|P(z)} μ(d)|A_d|, the inclusion-exclusion identity counting elements of A not divisible by primes below z, where P(z) = ∏_{p<z} p.

name: Twin prime sieve estimate
description: |{n ≤ x : n and n+2 both prime}| ≪ x/(log x)² by Selberg's or Brun's sieve, consistent with the Hardy–Littlewood conjecture up to the constant.

name: Additive character mod q
description: The function e_q(a) = e^{2πia/q} for a ∈ ℤ/qℤ, forming the character group of (ℤ/qℤ, +).

name: Orthogonality of additive characters
description: ∑_{a=0}^{q−1} e_q(na) = q if q|n and 0 otherwise, the discrete Fourier orthogonality for ℤ/qℤ.

name: Truncated Perron formula
description: ∑_{n≤x} aₙ = (1/2πi) ∫_{c−iT}^{c+iT} F(s)xˢ/s ds + O(xᶜ/(T·min(1,‖x‖))), the effective version of Perron's formula with explicit error from truncation.

name: Cesàro summability and Riesz means
description: The Riesz mean of order δ of a Dirichlet series: (1/Γ(δ+1)) ∑_{n≤x} aₙ(1−n/x)^δ, a smoothed partial sum that improves convergence properties.

name: Landau's formula for Dirichlet series coefficients
description: ∑_{n≤x} aₙ = (1/2πi) ∮ F(s)xˢ/s ds with the sum over residues giving the main terms, relating singularities of F(s) to the average behavior of aₙ.

name: 3-4-1 trigonometric inequality
description: 3 + 4cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0 for all real θ, the key inequality used to prove ζ(1+it) ≠ 0 via |ζ(σ)³ ζ(σ+it)⁴ ζ(σ+2it)| ≥ 1.

name: y-smooth integer (friable number)
description: A positive integer n is y-smooth if all its prime factors satisfy p ≤ y; Ψ(x,y) = |{n ≤ x : P⁺(n) ≤ y}| counts them.

name: Dickman rho function ρ(u)
description: The continuous function satisfying ρ(u) = 1 for 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 and uρ′(u) = −ρ(u−1) for u > 1, governing the density of smooth numbers: Ψ(x, x^{1/u}) ∼ ρ(u)x.

name: Smooth number asymptotic (de Bruijn / Hildebrand–Tenenbaum)
description: Ψ(x,y) ∼ xρ(u) uniformly for u = log x/log y in a wide range, with Hildebrand's refinement extending this to exp((log y)^{3/5−ε}) ≤ y ≤ x.

name: Buchstab function ω(u)
description: The continuous function with ω(u) = 1/u for 1 ≤ u ≤ 2 and (uω(u))′ = ω(u−1) for u > 2, arising in the Buchstab identity for Φ(x,y) = |{n ≤ x : P⁻(n) > y}|.

name: Primes in short intervals
description: π(x+h) − π(x) ∼ h/log x for h = x^θ with θ > 7/12 (Huxley), showing primes exist in intervals [x, x + x^θ].

name: Sathe–Selberg theorem on integers with k prime factors
description: |{n ≤ x : ω(n) = k}| ∼ (x/log x)(log log x)^{k−1}/((k−1)!) uniformly for 1 ≤ k ≤ (2−ε)log log x.

name: Beurling generalized primes
description: A sequence 1 < p₁ ≤ p₂ ≤ ⋯ of reals (generalized primes) generating by multiplicative closure a set of generalized integers; the framework for studying PNT-type results axiomatically.

name: Beurling PNT for generalized primes
description: If N(x) = Ax + O(x/(log x)^γ) with γ > 3/2 for the counting function of Beurling integers, then π_P(x) ∼ x/log x.

name: Induced Dirichlet character
description: Given χ a character mod q and q|Q, the character χ* mod Q defined by χ*(n) = χ(n) if gcd(n,Q) = 1 and 0 otherwise; every character is induced from a unique primitive character.

name: Quadratic Dirichlet character
description: A real-valued Dirichlet character of order 2, given by the Kronecker symbol χ_D(n) = (D/n) for a fundamental discriminant D.

name: Riemann hypothesis
description: All nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2; equivalently ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2+ε}) for every ε > 0.

name: Generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH)
description: All nontrivial zeros of every Dirichlet L-function L(s,χ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.

name: Hadamard product for ξ(s)
description: ξ(s) = ξ(0) ∏_ρ (1 − s/ρ), the product over nontrivial zeros ρ of ζ(s), obtained by applying the Hadamard factorization theorem to the entire function ξ(s) of order 1.

name: Zero-counting function N(T)
description: N(T) = |{ρ : ζ(ρ) = 0, 0 < Im(ρ) ≤ T}| = (T/2π)log(T/2πe) + O(log T), counting nontrivial zeros of ζ up to height T.

name: Classical zero-free region for L-functions
description: L(s,χ) ≠ 0 for σ > 1 − c/log(q(|t|+2)) with at most one exceptional real zero for real χ, extending de la Vallée Poussin's region to Dirichlet L-functions.

name: Siegel's theorem on L(1,χ)
description: For every ε > 0 there exists c(ε) > 0 (ineffective) such that L(1,χ) > c(ε)q^{−ε} for real primitive χ mod q, ruling out Siegel zeros in an ineffective sense.

name: Page's theorem
description: Among all real primitive characters χ mod q with q ≤ Q, at most one L(s,χ) can have a real zero β > 1 − c/log Q, and that exceptional modulus q₁ satisfies q₁ > Q^δ for some δ > 0.

name: Prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions
description: π(x;q,a) ∼ Li(x)/φ(q) for fixed q with gcd(a,q) = 1, with an error term depending on the zero-free region for L-functions mod q.

name: Siegel–Walfisz theorem
description: For any A > 0, ψ(x;q,a) = x/φ(q) + O(x exp(−c√(log x))) uniformly for q ≤ (log x)^A with gcd(a,q) = 1, using Siegel's ineffective zero-free region.

name: Vaughan's identity
description: Decomposes Λ(n) into Type I and Type II sums via Λ = μ_{≤U} ∗ log + μ_{≤U} ∗ Λ_{>V} ∗ 1 + remainder, enabling bilinear sum estimates in the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem and other applications.

name: Explicit formula for ψ(x;q,a)
description: ψ(x;q,a) = x/φ(q) − (1/φ(q)) ∑_χ ∑_ρ x^ρ/ρ + lower order terms, where ρ runs over nontrivial zeros of L(s,χ) for all χ mod q.

name: Weil's explicit formula
description: ∑_ρ h(ρ) = h(1) + h(0) − ∑_p ∑_k (log p / p^{k/2}) ĝ(k log p) + integral terms, relating a test function h evaluated at zeros of ζ to sums over primes.

name: Guinand–Weil explicit formula
description: A distributional identity ∑_ρ ĥ(γ_ρ) = ĥ(i/2) + ĥ(−i/2) − ∑_p log p ∑_k p^{−k/2}(h(k log p) + h(−k log p)) + integral terms, the symmetric form of Weil's explicit formula.

name: Von Koch's theorem: RH implies sharp prime counting
description: Under RH, π(x) = Li(x) + O(√x log x), equivalently ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2} log²x), the best possible error term up to logarithmic factors.

name: RH implies sharp error in arithmetic progressions
description: Under GRH, ψ(x;q,a) = x/φ(q) + O(x^{1/2} log²x) uniformly in q, giving the conditional analogue of von Koch's theorem for primes in AP.

name: Lindelöf hypothesis
description: ζ(1/2 + it) = O(|t|^ε) for every ε > 0, equivalent to μ(1/2) = 0 where μ(σ) is the infimum of exponents bounding |ζ(σ+it)|; implied by RH.

name: Conditional bounds on ζ(s) under RH
description: Under RH, |ζ(σ+it)| ≪ |t|^{(1−σ)/2+ε} for σ ≥ 1/2 and log|ζ(1/2+it)| ≪ log t/log log t, improving the unconditional convexity bound.

name: Conditional estimate for M(x) under RH
description: Under RH, M(x) = ∑_{n≤x} μ(n) = O(x^{1/2+ε}) for every ε > 0, the best conditional bound on the Mertens function.

name: Conditional bounds on gaps between primes under RH
description: Under RH, p_{n+1} − p_n ≪ √p_n log p_n, showing that consecutive prime gaps are O(√p log p).

name: Conditional estimate for π(x;q,a) with large q under GRH
description: Under GRH, π(x;q,a) = Li(x)/φ(q) + O(√x log x) for q ≤ x, effective for much larger moduli than unconditional results.

name: Zero density estimate N(σ,T)
description: N(σ,T) = |{ρ = β+iγ : L(ρ,χ) = 0, β ≥ σ, |γ| ≤ T}| ≪ T^{A(σ)(1−σ)+ε} for σ > 1/2, bounding zeros of L-functions away from the critical line.

name: Ingham density estimate
description: N(σ,T) ≪ T^{3(1−σ)/(2−σ)+ε} for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1, Ingham's classical zero density estimate for the Riemann zeta function.

name: Hardy's theorem on zeros on the critical line
description: ζ(s) has infinitely many zeros on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2 (Hardy, 1914).

name: Positive proportion of zeros on the critical line
description: At least 41.05% of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) lie on the critical line (Conrey, 1989), improving Selberg's result that a positive proportion do.

name: Density hypothesis
description: N(σ,T) ≪ T^{2(1−σ)+ε} for σ ≥ 1/2, a conjecture on the optimal exponent in zero density estimates, weaker than RH but sufficient for many applications.

name: Landau's oscillation theorem
description: If a Dirichlet series F(s) = ∑ aₙ/nˢ (aₙ real) has a singularity on the real axis at its abscissa of convergence σ_c, then ∑_{n≤x} aₙ oscillates in sign.

name: Ω₊/Ω₋ notation for oscillation
description: f(x) = Ω₊(g(x)) means lim sup f(x)/g(x) > 0; f(x) = Ω₋(g(x)) means lim inf f(x)/g(x) < 0; f(x) = Ω±(g(x)) means both hold.

name: Littlewood's omega theorem for π(x) − Li(x)
description: π(x) − Li(x) = Ω±(√x log log log x / log x), proving that Li(x) is not always an overestimate of π(x), despite being so for all computationally accessible x.

name: Oscillation of ψ(x) − x
description: ψ(x) − x = Ω±(√x), i.e. ψ(x) − x changes sign infinitely often and achieves magnitude at least c√x for some c > 0.

name: Omega result for M(x)
description: M(x) = Ω±(x^{1/2}), the Mertens function oscillates with amplitude at least c√x infinitely often.

name: Ingham's theorem on omega results from zeros
description: A general method producing Ω-results for summatory functions from knowledge of zeros of the associated Dirichlet series on the critical line.

name: Skewes number and sign changes of π(x) − Li(x)
description: The first x where π(x) > Li(x) exists (Littlewood); Skewes gave the first explicit upper bound, later improved to around e^{727.95} unconditionally.

name: Riemann–Stieltjes integral
description: ∫ₐᵇ f dα = lim ∑ f(tₖ)(α(xₖ) − α(xₖ₋₁)), generalizing the Riemann integral by integrating against a monotone or BV function α.

name: Integration by parts for Stieltjes integrals
description: ∫ₐᵇ f dα = fα|ₐᵇ − ∫ₐᵇ α df, the analogue of integration by parts for Riemann–Stieltjes integrals, fundamental for partial summation.

name: Values of ζ(s) at positive even integers
Weierstrass product for 1/Γ(z)
description: 1/Γ(z) = ze^{γz} ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1 + z/n)e^{−z/n}, the infinite product representation showing 1/Γ is entire of order 1.

name: Theta function (number-theoretic)
description: ϑ(t) = ∑_{n=−∞}^{∞} e^{−πn²t} for t > 0, equal to θ₃(0, e^{−πt}) in Jacobi notation, central to the proof of the functional equation of ζ(s).

name: Theta function transformation formula
description: ϑ(1/t) = √t · ϑ(t) for t > 0, a consequence of Poisson summation, used to derive the functional equation of the Riemann zeta function.

name: Rankin's trick
description: Bounding a counting function ∑_{n≤x} aₙ by (x/y)^δ ∑_{n≤y} aₙ(n/y)^{−δ} for a free parameter δ > 0, converting a sharp cutoff into a smooth weight.

name: Dirichlet's divisor problem
description: Determine the infimum α such that ∑_{n≤x} d(n) = x log x + (2γ−1)x + O(x^α); conjectured α = 1/4, best known α ≈ 0.314 (Kolesnik, Huxley).

name: Selberg class
description: An axiomatic class S of Dirichlet series satisfying: (i) analytic continuation, (ii) Ramanujan bound on coefficients, (iii) functional equation, (iv) Euler product; conjectured to coincide with automorphic L-functions.

name: Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region
description: ζ(σ+it) ≠ 0 for σ > 1 − c/(log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}, a wider zero-free region than de la Vallée Poussin's, obtained via exponential sum estimates.

name: Mertens conjecture (disproved)
description: |M(x)| < √x for all x > 1 was conjectured by Mertens; disproved by Odlyzko and te Riele (1985) using computations of zeros of ζ(s).

name: Twin prime conjecture
description: There are infinitely many primes p such that p+2 is also prime; unproven, though Zhang (2013) proved bounded gaps between primes.

name: Hardy–Littlewood twin prime conjecture
description: |{p ≤ x : p+2 prime}| ∼ 2C₂ x/(log x)² where C₂ = ∏_{p≥3}(1−1/(p−1)²) ≈ 0.6602 is the twin prime constant.

name: Dirichlet series for the Liouville function
description: ∑_{n=1}^∞ λ(n)/nˢ = ζ(2s)/ζ(s) for Re(s) > 1, expressing the Dirichlet series of Liouville's function via zeta.

name: Ramanujan's sum formula for σ_s(n)
description: σ_s(n)/n^s = ζ(s+1) ∑_{q=1}^∞ c_q(n)/q^{s+1}, expressing the divisor function as an absolutely convergent series of Ramanujan sums.

name: Vinogradov–Korobov error term in PNT
description: ψ(x) = x + O(x exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{−1/5})), the best known unconditional error term in the PNT.

name: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture
description: The pair correlation of normalized spacings of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) follows 1 − (sin πu/(πu))² (GUE statistics), connecting zeros of zeta to random matrix theory.

name: Explicit formula with general test function
description: A general identity ∑_ρ h(ρ) = δ + ∫ h·K − ∑_p ∑_k g(k log p) log p / p^{k/2} for suitable test functions h with Fourier transform g, unifying various explicit formulas.

name: Halász's theorem
description: For multiplicative f with |f(n)| ≤ 1, (1/x)∑_{n≤x} f(n) = O(exp(−c min_|t|≤T ∑_{p≤x}(1−Re f(p)p^{−it})/p)) + O(1/T), characterizing when mean values of multiplicative functions are small.

name: Generalized von Mangoldt function Λ_k
description: Λ_k = μ ∗ log^k, the k-fold Dirichlet convolution giving Λ₁ = Λ and Λ_k(n) supported on integers with at most k prime factors; −ζ^(k)(s)/ζ(s) = ∑ Λ_k(n)/nˢ.

name: Grand Riemann hypothesis
description: All nontrivial zeros of all automorphic L-functions lie on Re(s) = 1/2, the strongest form of RH encompassing Dedekind zeta, Artin L-functions, and all automorphic L-functions.

name: Effective vs ineffective constants
description: A constant is effective if it can in principle be computed; ineffective if its existence is proved indirectly (e.g., via Siegel's theorem). The distinction is central to the gap between Siegel–Walfisz and Bombieri–Vinogradov.

name: Riemann–Stieltjes partial summation technique
description: Converting ∑_{n≤x} f(n)g(n) into ∫₁ˣ g(t) dA(t) where A(t) = ∑_{n≤t} f(n), then integrating by parts to separate smooth and arithmetic parts.

name: Dirichlet series multiplication theorem
description: If F(s) = ∑ f(n)/nˢ and G(s) = ∑ g(n)/nˢ converge absolutely, then F(s)G(s) = ∑ (f∗g)(n)/nˢ where f∗g is the Dirichlet convolution.

name: Explicit zero-free region constant improvements
description: Numerical improvements to the classical zero-free region σ > 1 − 1/(R log t) for ζ(s), with the best explicit R values due to Ford, Kadiri, and others.
